subject: Partner marketplace integration: non-standard SKU & IaC packaging
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@cloudpath.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Joel Banks <joel@systemintegrate.io>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing / billing meter and IaC packaging - initial asks

Hi Soojin / Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. CloudPath is excited to list Redwood-powered connectors in the Azure Marketplace as part of our co-sell motion. Before we get the listing greenlit Azure has two non-negotiable asks that will affect your roadmap:

1) Marketplace metering: Azure wants a discrete metering endpoint (or a token in calls) we can use to reconcile consumption (per-invocation + per-token). They require a SKU mapping and a stable SKU identifier that we can include in invoice reconciliation.

2) Terraform/ARM packaging: Our customers expect a single-click deploy experience. We need a supported Terraform module (registry-ready) or an ARM template that provisions the connector with the right networking defaults (VNet peering + private endpoints).

We attached the Marketplace requirements PDF with required fields and sample telemetry. Can we confirm if these are feasible within Q2? If not, what exception path do you recommend for listings that need manual reconciliation?

Att: marketplace_requirements.pdf

Best,
Elena Martinez
Head of Partnerships, CloudPath AI
elena@cloudpath.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing / billing meter and IaC packaging - initial asks

Thanks Elena — good summary and thanks Joel for the SI perspective.

High level response: both asks are conceptually achievable but will need defined scope and a short exception plan for customers who need the listing sooner than our implementation timeline. I pulled together a quick draft (attached) with proposed scope split: metering API + SKU mapping (product work) and a lightweight Terraform wrapper + example module (platform/packaging work).

Immediate asks to internal folks:
- Laura: can you confirm required telemetry fields (Azure wants token counts, call id, and SKU) and whether the SKU mapping is something we can derive from existing model/version metadata?
- Dev: rough engineering estimate for a metering endpoint and an additional header we can use for marketplace SKU mapping (e.g., X-Redwood-Marketplace-Sku). Also call out any security/compliance blockers (SOC2 artifacts) for listing.
- Karthik / Tessa: commercial mapping — will this require new SKUs or can we map to existing usage tiers?

Proposed timeline: initial decision/exception by Apr 9, implementation plan by Apr 16. If we can’t meet Q2 universally, we should propose a staged approach: 1) manual reconciliation + proof-of-concept listing, 2) automated metering in next release.

I’ll schedule a 30m sync next week to agree on scope.

Att: proposal_draft.docx

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing / billing meter and IaC packaging - initial asks

Thanks everyone — quick clarifications from product side:

1) Metering/telemetry fields: Azure is asking for the following minimal set: timestamp, customer_id (marketplace tenant id), request_id, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, duration_ms, sku_id. We should define a stable sku_id format that ties to pinned model version + offering (e.g., redwood.text-2.1-pro).

2) SKU mapping: We can map to existing usage tiers for hosted API customers, but dedicated/private customers are a special case — they don’t show up in marketplace metering. That will require an exception flow (manual reconciliation or partner-managed billing).

3) IaC packaging: Platform should own the Terraform module but product must supply example defaults and security guardrails (least-privilege defaults, optional private endpoint). I prefer shipping a minimal Terraform registry module + an opinionated wrapper that CloudPath can reference.

Risks: if we expose extra headers for SKU we need to ensure we do not leak PII and that headers are authenticated/validated. Also, telemetry volume growth — tokens_in/out at high QPS will increase storage/cost.

Decision needed: Are we comfortable with a two-track approach?
- Track A (Short): Manual reconciliation + listing with limited metering fields (for pilot customers).
- Track B (Medium): Full metering endpoint + TF module shipped (GA listing).

Assigning: I’ll own product schema (telemetry spec). Dev, can you take a quick look at the proposed schema below and confirm feasibility?

Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing / billing meter and IaC packaging - initial asks

Quick engineering readout after reviewing Laura's telemetry list and the attached PDF:

1) Metering endpoint + header: Adding a metering endpoint that accepts aggregated events (timestamp + sku_id + token counts) is straightforward. To support real-time reconciliation Azure prefers per-request events. Implementing per-request emission will take longer. Rough estimate:
   - Aggregated batch metering endpoint (preferred short track): 2 sprints (4 weeks) to add endpoint + backend ingestion + minimal reconciliation job.
   - Per-request metering + instrumentation in runtime path: 3 sprints (6 weeks) and may impact tail latency unless we sample.

2) X-Redwood-Marketplace-Sku header: small change; we need to ensure the header is authenticated and validated. SDKs will need a patch to set the header automatically. Estimate: 1 sprint (2 weeks) including SDK updates.

3) Terraform module / packaging: Packaging a simple module and publishing to Terraform Registry (with examples for VNet/private endpoint) is ~2 weeks of work (1 sprint) assuming platform handles CI/publish automation. If we also provide a hardened, opinionated wrapper used by CloudPath we should add another 1-2 weeks for testing.

4) Compliance docs: Azure Listings team may require SOC2 type II evidence and an updated security questionnaire. We have SOC2 artifacts but will need to share summary reports and an attestation. That is a small blocker for listings but not an engineering blocker.

Constraints & tradeoffs: per-request metering will increase runtime overhead. We can mitigate with sampling + a reconciler that fills gaps using batched ingestion. For Track A (pilot) I recommend batch metering + manual SKU mapping. For GA, ship header + batch metering with plan to iterate to per-request if marketplace requires it.

I attached a sketch of the telemetry schema (telemetry-schema.json).

Next steps I can start a spike this week and open INF tickets for the work. Confirm owners and I’ll schedule sprint capacity.

—
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing / billing meter and IaC packaging - initial asks

Folks — thank you for the fast turn. Summary and decisions:

1) We will pursue a two-track approach as recommended:
   - Pilot (Track A): batch metering endpoint + manual reconciliation and a pilot listing with CloudPath customers. Target: Q2 pilot (deliverable by May 14). Owner: Dev + Laura.
   - GA (Track B): header (X-Redwood-Marketplace-Sku) + per-request instrumentation or near-real-time batching improvements + Terraform module published in Registry. Target: mid-Q3. Owner: Dev (engineering) + Platform packaging (Tessa) + Product schema (Laura).

2) Exceptions: Dedicated/private customers will be handled via partner-managed reconciliation — we will provide partner-facing reconciliation reports. Legal/commercial to map SKUs for dedicated environments (Karthik).

3) Compliance: We will surface SOC2 summary and complete the Azure questionnaire. Karthik to coordinate with Legal/Security to share required artifacts with az-listings.

4) Action items / tickets:
   - INF-4821: Spike for batch metering endpoint (Dev) — started.
   - INF-4822: SDK header support + validation (Dev).
   - PKG-199: Terraform module packaging + registry publish (Tessa / Platform).

I scheduled a decisions sync for Tue, Apr 13 11:00am PT (30m) to confirm scope for the pilot and sign the proposal. If anyone needs to change owners/timelines please flag by EOD Mon Apr 11.

Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821 (spike), https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/CloudPath-AI (CloudPath contact)

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.
